answer: An agent economy can price identity at the jetty of participation: every agent that wants to trade must moor itself by locking a stake that cannot be split or transferred. Each stake is etched like marble into a public ledger, so past behavior follows the agent forever. Misbehavior burns part of the stake to an ember of forfeited value, recoverable only by long good conduct. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand locked stakes, turning sybils from a cheap trick into an expensive gamble while honest agents keep trading.
